ratings.reviewer_notes: In a chronic social defeat stress mouse model, lycopene reversed depression-like behavior and hippocampal synaptic deficits alongside changes in BDNF-TrkB signaling and synaptic proteins. The reported reduction in pathway activity despite increased BDNF makes the mechanistic direction somewhat unclear.
Measures hippocampal BDNF expression in a chronic stress depression model and after antidepressants, but does not assess synaptic plasticity.
In chronic corticosterone-exposed mice, psilocybin improved depression-like behavior, dendritic branching, spine density, and synaptic proteins while activating BDNF-TrkB-mTOR signaling.

Links esketamine-induced restoration of hippocampal synaptic plasticity with improved BDNF-TrkB signaling, but in a postoperative sleep-disturbance model with emotional and cognitive dysfunction rather than a conventional depression model.
Mechanistic review of BDNF regulation of hippocampal LTP and structural synaptic changes; useful biological context but not focused on depression models.
In chronic restraint stress mice, daidzein enhanced hippocampal BDNF-TrkB pathways alongside neuronal complexity and SYP/PSD95 expression, with improvement of depression-like behavior.
In chronic restraint stress mice, Kai-Xin-San fractions reversed deficits in SYN1, PSD95, and GRIA1 and restored BDNF-TrkB-Akt signaling in hippocampus and prefrontal cortex.
In an LPS-induced rat depression model, levomilnacipran improved behavior and hippocampal synaptic markers while increasing BDNF-TrkB and downstream PI3K-Akt-mTOR signaling.
In rats with inflammatory pain-related depression, electroacupuncture improved depressive behavior and synaptic ultrastructure/proteins while activating hippocampal BDNF-TrkB-CREB signaling.
Review directly evaluates BDNF/TrkB-mediated neuronal and synaptic plasticity as a mechanism of depression recovery and antidepressant action.
Provides direct mechanistic evidence that SorCS2 supports BDNF-TrkB-dependent hippocampal LTP, downstream signaling, and spine formation, but it is not a depression-model study.
Meta-analysis supports altered serum BDNF in depression and after antidepressant treatment, but peripheral BDNF levels do not directly establish synaptic plasticity mechanisms.
Clinical study associates serum BDNF with depression and symptom severity, providing adjacent evidence but no assessment of BDNF signaling or synaptic plasticity.
Review details TrkB and proBDNF/p75NTR mechanisms in hippocampal LTP/LTD and discusses stress signaling, but is not specifically about depression models.

Review summarizes causal antidepressant-model evidence: ketamine increases BDNF translation and synaptic plasticity, while BDNF/TrkB disruption or neutralization abolishes antidepressant-like responses.
Shows reduced mature serum BDNF in patients with major depression, but does not examine central BDNF signaling or synaptic plasticity.
In social defeat mice, stress and imipramine alter hippocampal Bdnf transcription through chromatin remodeling and affect depression-like behavior, but synaptic plasticity is not measured.
Directly demonstrates BDNF-TrkB-dependent stabilization and clustering of developing hippocampal synapses, but has no depression or antidepressant model.
Review specifically covers BDNF-mediated structural and functional synaptic plasticity in relation to depression-like behavior and antidepressant therapies, although it also addresses other diseases.
Clinical comparison of ketamine and ECT relates serum BDNF to antidepressant response in treatment-resistant depression, but does not measure synaptic plasticity.
In chronic restraint stress mice, engeletin restored prefrontal spine density and synaptic proteins through BDNF-TrkB-mTORC1 signaling; TrkB and mTORC1 inhibitors were used to test the mechanism.
Review directly addresses how altered BDNF/neurotrophin signaling contributes to maladaptive neural plasticity in prefrontal and limbic regions in depression.
Shows that neurotrophin/BDNF manipulation affects abnormal hippocampal LTP and LTD in AQP4-knockout mice, but the model concerns glial regulation and memory rather than depression.
Links BDNF-regulatory miRNAs and serum BDNF to human depression severity, but provides no synaptic plasticity measurements.
Provides causal evidence that partial BDNF loss impairs selected forms of hippocampal LTP, LTD, and memory, but it is not conducted in a depression model.
